audit_scope: Read-only trace of the ACT fork's data and training path before any edit.
traced_path: task_config supplies dataset_dir, num_episodes, episode_len, camera_names
state_dim/action_dim chosen by a hard-coded task-name allowlist (imitate_episodes.py:62-73)
utils.load_data(dataset_dir, num_episodes, camera_names, bs, bs, chunk_size)
ACTPolicy truncates actions/is_pad to num_queries, masks L1 with ~is_pad
train_bc: per-epoch validation, then training; best kept by deepcopy(state_dict)
policy_best.ckpt written at end of main() from best_ckpt_info

act_generates_its_own_random_split.evidence: utils.py:121 shuffled_indices = np.random.permutation(num_episodes); :122-123 slice at int(0.8*N).
act_generates_its_own_random_split.note: Ignores any committed split entirely. Also seeded by set_seed(1) in main(), not by --seed, because load_data runs before train_bc's set_seed(seed).

normalization_uses_all_100_episodes.evidence: imitate_episodes.py:147 load_data(...) -> utils.py:126 get_norm_stats(dataset_dir, num_episodes) with num_episodes=100; utils.py:87 iterates range(num_episodes).
normalization_uses_all_100_episodes.note: Validation trajectories contribute to qpos/action mean and std. This is normalization leakage and must be restricted to the 80 training trajectories.

dataset_files_discovered_by_filesystem_o.evidence: utils.py:28 and :88 build the path as f'episode_{episode_id}.hdf5' from an integer index; no glob or listdir is used.
dataset_files_discovered_by_filesystem_o.note: Good: no filesystem-order dependence. The risk here is the contiguity assumption below, not ordering.

episode_ids_assumed_contiguous.evidence: utils.py:87 for episode_idx in range(num_episodes); indices come from np.random.permutation(num_episodes).
episode_ids_assumed_contiguous.note: The converted canonical dataset is exactly episode_0..episode_99 (verified contiguous), so the assumption holds. It still must not be the mechanism that defines the split.

validation_dataloader_is_shuffled.note: Validation order is nondeterministic, so per-epoch validation loss is not reproducible. Must be shuffle=False.

qpos_action_statistics_include_padded_ti.evidence: utils.py:90-92 reads root['/observations/qpos'][()] and root['/action'][()] — the full on-disk arrays, which contain only real timesteps. Padding is created later, per sample, in __getitem__.
qpos_action_statistics_include_padded_ti.note: Padding does not contaminate the statistics. The only statistics defect is the episode set.

variable_length_episode_padding.answer: padded to num_queries (chunk size), not to episode_len
variable_length_episode_padding.evidence: utils.py:55-59 padded_action = zeros((num_queries, action_dim)); n_real = min(action_len, num_queries); is_pad[n_real:] = 1.
variable_length_episode_padding.note: This fork already diverges from upstream ACT (which pads to episode_len). Padding to num_queries is what the batch contract for this task requires, and truncation past num_queries is harmless because the model only predicts num_queries steps.

all_batch_elements_receive_same_action_s.evidence: padded_action is always (num_queries, action_dim) and is_pad is always (num_queries,), independent of episode length or start_ts.
all_batch_elements_receive_same_action_s.note: Heterogeneous episode lengths therefore batch correctly with default collation.

sim_attribute_set_correctly.evidence: Converter writes dst.attrs['sim'] = True; utils.py:30 reads root.attrs.get('sim', False). All 100 converted episodes verified sim=True.
sim_attribute_set_correctly.note: EpisodicDataset.is_sim is a side effect of the most recent __getitem__ and is initialised by calling __getitem__(0) in __init__ (utils.py:19). Fragile, but correct for a homogeneous sim dataset.

simulation_actions_begin_at_same_timeste.evidence: utils.py:44-46 with is_sim True: action = root['/action'][start_ts:], action_len = episode_len - start_ts.
simulation_actions_begin_at_same_timeste.note: Observation at t is paired with the action sequence beginning at t, which is the required simulation alignment.

non_simulation_start_ts_minus_1_hack_act.evidence: utils.py:48-49 is the else branch of `if is_sim`; sim=True on every converted episode so the max(0, start_ts - 1) path is never taken.
non_simulation_start_ts_minus_1_hack_act.note: Confirmed inactive for this dataset, as required.

state_dimension_hard_coded.evidence: imitate_episodes.py:62-73 sets state_dim by matching task_name against a literal allowlist; 'obstacle_baseline' is in the branch giving state_dim = 9.
state_dimension_hard_coded.note: Correct value for this dataset, but derived from a task-name string rather than the data. Should be made explicit and asserted against the H5.

action_dimension_hard_coded.note: Correct value; should be asserted against the H5.

camera_names_hard_coded.note: Correct for this dataset. Must be asserted against the H5 image groups.

episode_horizon_hard_coded.note: episode_len 169 belongs to the OLD invalid obstacle_v1 collection; the canonical dataset needs 132. dataset_dir is a machine-specific absolute path on another host pointing at the superseded dataset. episode_len is not used by the training data path (only by eval_bc as max_timesteps), but it must still be corrected and must not be the mechanism that selects the dataset.

checkpoint_resume_preserves_optimizer_an.evidence: train_bc (imitate_episodes.py:366-470) has no resume path. Periodic saves at epoch % 100 == 0 write torch.save(policy.state_dict()) only — no optimizer state, no RNG state, no epoch counter, no best-so-far record. Saves are not atomic (direct torch.save to the final path).
checkpoint_resume_preserves_optimizer_an.note: An interrupted 2000-epoch run cannot be resumed without repeating work and losing optimizer/RNG continuity.

proximity_consumed.evidence: detr/main.py:78 n_proximity_sensors default 0, which the comment states makes the model bit-identical to vanilla ACT; policy.py passes proximity_positions=None; --use_proximity not set.
proximity_consumed.note: Vanilla ACT baseline confirmed: no proximity tokens, no extra Linear layer.

safety_cvae_loaded.evidence: imitate_episodes.py imports only constants, utils, policy, visualize_episodes; hybrid_safety_residual is a separate module never imported on the training path.

optimizer_behavior_recorded_not_changed.lr_schedule: none applied during training (lr_drop parsed but unused)

loss_definition_recorded_not_changed.l1: F.l1_loss(actions, a_hat, reduction='none') masked by ~is_pad then .mean()
loss_definition_recorded_not_changed.note: L1 is correctly masked so padded timesteps do not contribute to the loss.

blocking_defects_summary: random 80/20 split replaces any committed split (utils.py:121)
normalization statistics computed over all 100 episodes, leaking the 20 validation trajectories (utils.py:126)
validation DataLoader shuffled, making validation loss nonreproducible (utils.py:132)
constants.py obstacle_baseline points at a machine-specific absolute path for the superseded obstacle_v1 dataset with episode_len 169 instead of 132
no optimizer/RNG/epoch resume state and non-atomic checkpoint writes
non_defects_confirmed: simulation temporal alignment is correct and the start_ts-1 real-robot hack is inactive
padding produces a uniform (num_queries, action_dim) action tensor and a matching mask, so heterogeneous lengths batch correctly
padded timesteps do not enter the normalization statistics
padded timesteps do not enter the L1 loss
episode files are not discovered by filesystem order
no proximity input and no Safety-CVAE on the training path
verdict_note: Five blocking defects. All are confined to the data/training path (utils.py, imitate_episodes.py, constants.py) and none require touching the ACT architecture, loss, KL formulation, chunking or optimizer mathematics.
